title: Production prompt cohort synthesis and rarity-aware sampling for quantization validation
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a repeatable, per-domain calibration dataset construction process that mixes production replay with synthesized variants and a rarity-aware oversampling strategy. The goal is to generate compact 'validation cohorts' for FP8/INT8 calibration that reflect real production distributions while amplifying rare but high-impact cases so quantization regressions are caught early.
background: We currently use large replay-derived packs for calibration but observe two failure modes: (1) low-occurrence but high-impact prompts (legal/financial/PHI-like) are underrepresented and cause accuracy regressions under aggressive quantization; (2) timestamped or near-duplicate prompts bloat packs and reduce coverage efficiency. Prior tickets explored per-domain packs and stratified reservoir sampling, but we need an approach that explicitly synthesizes edge variants and weights rarity by measured sensitivity between float and quantized model outputs.
proposal: Build a pipeline that: (A) identifies domain cohorts via metadata and semantic clusters; (B) selects a base replay sample per cohort using timestamp-decayed reservoir sampling; (C) computes a rarity score combining absolute frequency, semantic distance to nearest cluster centroid, and token-loss delta between float and a candidate quantized model on a small probe set; (D) synthesizes variants for rare items using constrained paraphrasing (beam-constrained editing) and context-anchored substitutions; (E) constructs the final pack by importance-sampling with a configurable tail-weight parameter so rare/high-sensitivity items are oversampled up to Xx relative to baseline frequency.
sampling_algorithm: Steps: 1) Ingest production prompts with domain tag and fingerprint (sha1 of normalized text). 2) Deduplicate exact matches within a rolling 90-day window; keep the earliest timestamp for cohort diversity. 3) Build semantic clusters per domain using an embedding index (approxNN, 128-d) with k tuned per domain (k=50..400). 4) For each prompt compute: frequency f, centroid_distance d, and sensitivity s = KL(float || quant) or token-loss delta on a 256-token probe. 5) Rarity score r = alpha*(1/f) + beta*(d_norm) + gamma*(s_norm) where alpha,beta,gamma are tunable. 6) Apply timestamp decay weight w_t = exp(-lambda * age_days) to prefer recent usage. 7) Importance sample N_base items per domain proportional to r * w_t, then generate M_synth synthetic variants for top-k rare items using constrained paraphraser. 8) Final pack assembly: cap per-user-origin to avoid single-customer skew, enforce token-length buckets (<=64, 65-256, >256) to match runtime seq-length distribution. 9) Output canonical pack with provenance metadata and per-item weight used for sampling.
dataset_targets: Per-domain pack size target: min 2k items, target 10k items, max 30k items. Tail amplification: rare items should constitute 20-35% of the pack (configurable). Aim for 70/20/10 distribution across length buckets (short/medium/long) where possible.
evaluation_metrics: Accuracy regression delta (float -> quant) measured by: 1) mean token-level log-loss change; 2) generation ROUGE / BLEU on labeled eval subsets; 3) structural correctness checks for function calling outputs; 4) downstream task exact-match for deterministic tasks; 5) false-positive/negative rate change for safety classifiers. Track 95th-percentile latency and per-token variance only as side metrics.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Pipeline generates per-domain packs for three pilot domains (support-chat, invoices, developer-qa) that meet target sizes. 2) On the assembled packs, the selected FP8 quantized model must not degrade task-level exact-match by >1.5% absolute for any pilot domain compared to float baseline. 3) Rare-case recall: manually curated list of 120 high-risk prompts across domains must be present or covered by synthesized variants >= 90% of the time. 4) Pack generation time < 2 hours for a 10k-item pack on dedicated builder infra. 5) Pack includes provenance (source id, timestamp, synthesis method) and sampling weights.
progress_updates: 2025-11-05: scoped algorithm and tuned rarity formula; alpha/beta/gamma initial values = 0.5/0.3/0.2 for pilot runs.
2025-11-08: implemented embedding-based clustering prototype (Faiss HNSW) and verified cluster sizes per domain; support-chat clusters dense, invoices more sparse.
2025-11-12: added small probe harness to compute token-loss delta between float and INT8 candidate; discovered several prompt patterns with >3% token-loss increases — flagged as high-sensitivity.
2025-11-15: integrated constrained paraphraser (beam=4, constraint set derived from named-entity mask) to synthesize variants; initial quality spot-checked by SEs.
2025-11-20: assembled pilot packs for support-chat (8.6k), invoices (3.1k), developer-qa (6.4k). Running quant validation suite overnight.
decisions: Use embedding-centroid distance as a proxy for novelty instead of raw n-gram rarity because semantics matter for model sensitivity.
Cap synthetic variants at 3 per seed prompt to avoid hallucination drift; prefer paraphrase+entity-preserve edits.
Tune timestamp decay lambda per domain; e.g., support-chat lambda = 0.004 (favors recent), invoices lambda = 0.001 (longer tail).
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Synthesized variants may introduce distributional mismatch (hallucinations) leading to false positives. Mitigation: constrained paraphrasing and automatic NER-preservation checks; human spot checks on top-200 synthesized items.

Risk: Over-amplifying rare items could bias calibration and increase average-case error. Mitigation: keep an explicit budget cap and validate aggregate loss metrics; run ablation comparing balanced vs tail-amplified packs.
Risk: Single-customer skew. Mitigation: enforce per-origin caps and label items with origin_id for audits.
Risk: Computational cost of probe sensitivity measurement. Mitigation: amortize by running probes on a 2k-item stratified sample rather than whole corpus; cache results for repeated runs.
Risk: Privacy-sensitive prompts. Mitigation: filter PHI signatures, apply redaction pipeline, and require security_review for any pack containing remnants; maintain redaction provenance tags.
